Sibuna v0.3.3 fixes console diagnostics and the recovery-code screen after two-factor
setup. Request inspection, CRS decisions and wire protocols are unchanged from v0.3.2.

Fixes:
- An unsupported console schema now reports CONSOLESCHEMA. The hint asks operators to
  keep the data directory and use compatible binaries. It no longer suggests a quorum outage.
- Invalid input, permission refusals, stale revisions and storage outages have distinct
  hints, shared by the HTTP service and Wasm interface. After a write timeout, operators
  are told to read the saved state before retrying.
- In v0.3.2, successful two-factor confirmation revoked the session, but the interface
  switched to sign-in before showing the ten recovery codes. The codes now remain on a
  standalone result screen until the user saves them. This screen has no dashboard access
  or telemetry stream. A late revocation callback cannot erase the new codes.
- Confirmation and disabling two-factor clear the previous account view. Failed attempts
  resume the authenticated stream without changing the factor or its replay checks.

Upgrade:
- The console schema remains at version 46. No migration is added in this release.
- When upgrading from a release older than v0.3.2, upgrade every cluster node. Older binaries
  cannot use schema 46. Do not downgrade or edit its version marker.
- Retain the console key file, and give every console node the same key.

Qualification:
- Native storage tests cover newer and invalid schema markers, migration rollback and
  typed startup failures. HTTP and Wasm tests distinguish refusals from storage outages.
- A live daemon and the shipped Wasm complete enrollment, save the recovery codes, sign in,
  replace the codes and disable two-factor. The test also injects a late revocation callback.
- The Linux regression gate passed all 95 build steps. It executed 568 tests successfully;
  other unchanged tests were cached. Book and SID builds passed, and affected pages were
  inspected after rendering.
- Chrome reproduced the v0.3.2 recovery-screen defect. The final binary then showed all
  ten codes, cleared them after saving and returned to sign-in. Recovery replacement and
  disabling were also checked, including a narrow layout. Desktop emulation was restored.
- The release workflow qualifies each packaged executable before publication. A twelve-hour
  single-node and three-host functional soak will start after publication. Its results are
  separate from these release checks and from performance acceptance.
- No measured request subsystem changed. Existing benchmark records remain tied to their
  recorded commits. The SID 0007 performance exception remains; this release does not
  claim that the strict console-impact gate passed.

Downloads:
- Linux x86-64 and ARM64: statically linked musl builds; Linux 5.10 or later.
- macOS Apple Silicon and Intel: macOS 15 or later; unsigned command-line builds.
- Windows x86-64: native sibuna.exe; Windows 10 / Server 2019 or later.

Archives include the executable, README, license texts, dependency notices and an exact
build manifest. SHA256SUMS covers every archive. Engine sources are LGPL-3.0; console
sources, including the Wasm interface, are AGPL-3.0. The combined executable is AGPL-covered.
CRS rules are Apache-2.0 and are downloaded and verified at runtime, not bundled.
Corresponding source and build scripts are in this release's tag and linked from the console.
Companies seeking alternative licensing can contact the authors, Vikrant Rathore and
Ronak Rathore. Third-party libraries remain subject to their respective licenses.

The shipped builds include storage and console support; the console starts with --console.
Multi-node deployments require a separate -Dcluster=true build with OpenSSL 3. No GeoIP address
database is bundled; use the documented CLI import/update commands for your chosen dataset.

The v0.3.0 release notes describe the earlier behaviour changes and deployment limits:
https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/releases/tag/v0.3.0

Documentation: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/
Deployment guide: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/book/operations.html
